title: WearOS 'Apps on Your Phone' support being depricated by Google - XDrip WearOS functionality becoming un-usable
body:
Google is terminating support for Android-app-bundled WearOS watch-apps in-favor of requiring all watch-apps to be hosted on the Play Store.

XDrip uses the 'old method' (watch app bundled inside phone version), which means that XDrip WearOS support will break for new installs (and re-installs), as it will not be possible to install the WearOS xdrip app anymore.

Fix involves either:
A) breaking-out the WearOS app into it's own separately downloadable APK and posting it along with instructions on how to adb-sideload it *to the watch*
-or-
B) Getting it listed on the play-store.

Okay, I will also attempt to adapt the existing xDrip wear installer component to use adb, so once it is installed the first time it can self update.

I've added this in the April 13th Nightly which is available now.

So for the updated version the instructions are as follows:

- Install the latest nightly xDrip WearOs component to the watch, eg using Wear Installer app, downgrading play store or via adb manually. 
- Make sure developer mode is enabled on the Watch
- Make sure that wifi adb debugging is enabled
- Go to xDrip Prefs on the Watch, scroll till you see `Force Update` - tap it
- It should check ADB, and ask for authorization, select `Always Allow`
- Probably it will tell you ADB isn't working due to needing the authorization 
- Go in to xDrip Prefs again on the watch and click Force Update
- This time it should say ADB looks good and then ask xDrip phone app to send the latest version
- This should download and then xDrip will install itself.

Because the versions are currently identical then this wont really do much, but this process can be used to force xDrip to send the latest version in future but it should also automatically detect version changes and update in the background. For fun you could install the latest nightly on the watch then downgrade your phone and check that the update process then downgrades your watch app version. The version information should be displayed next to the `Force Update` text.

The idea is that you no longer need to use Wear Installer or whatever method you used to install the first time around (eg PC based adb or downgrading play store) as xDrip can update itself.

Please also remember the not so tech-savvy users. 
I know a few users, that are from the older generation, who won't be able to follow those steps at all. 
So everything that's beyong "enable dev mode and enable adb debugging" is from my feeling a real blocker for everyone who is not into tech stuff...

@xannasavin  Yes ADB wifi debugging is used by xDrip to update the watch app. Is there a reason you want to turn it off?
Well, to my knowledge it's a security concern, but I might be wrong. However, since I update xDrip manually anyways, I can enable it just before updating xDrip I guess...?

@xannasavin  If a rogue device tried to connect to your adb on your watch then your watch would pop up asking for permission first. Each client device trying to use adb has its own set of security keys, you have to approve each different device. With xDrip connecting to the adb bridge internally it generates a key the first time and uses that again each time. So after you have first approved xDrip's access with the `Always Allow` option then you wont get asked again, so if it pops up asking for permission then you'd know if it were something else.  Adb is normally only considered a security risk in that a user could just hit approve without knowing what it was for or if it bypassed the lock screen.
